title.value: Gradient based sample selection for online continual learning
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the paper, both on the cover page and in the header of introductory sections.
title.quote: Gradient based sample selection for online continual learning

analysis.description: This research paper addresses the issue of catastrophic forgetting in neural networks for continual learning. It introduces a method of sample selection for replay buffers formulated as a constraint reduction problem, aiming to maximize sample diversity using gradient parameters as features. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in continual learning benchmarks.

type.justification: The paper demonstrates empirical evaluations using continual learning benchmarks, measuring the effectiveness of the proposed sample selection method compared to other strategies.
type.quote: We perform experiments on continual learning benchmarks and show that our method is on par with, or better than, the previous methods.

name.justification: The paper primarily discusses methodologies and strategies to tackle continual learning problems, explicitly aiming to improve sample selection for replay buffers in this context.
name.quote: A continual learning agent learns online with a non-stationary and never-ending stream of data.

name.justification: A significant portion of the paper deals with addressing catastrophic forgetting in the context of continual learning.
name.quote: The key to such learning process is to overcome the catastrophic forgetting of previously seen data, which is a well known problem of neural networks.

name.justification: GEM is explicitly mentioned as a method being compared against in experiments related to continual learning benchmarks.
name.quote: Recent works that use replay buffer for continual learning include iCaRL [14] and GEM [10]

is_contributed.justification: GEM is a referenced model used for comparison and not a contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: Recent works that use replay buffer for continual learning include iCaRL [14] and GEM [10]
